title: Isolation and culturing of primary mouse astrocytes for the analysis of focal adhesion dynamics
protocol: Place 10 mL of 1× HBSS in a 15 mL Falcon tube on ice.
Place 1 mL of 0.05% DNase I and 1 mL of 0.05% trypsin on ice.
Arrange dissection tools, microscope, cold light source, and 70% ethanol under the dissection hood.
Gently hold the mice pup.
Spray the neck with 70% ethanol to prevent contamination.
Decapitate the mouse using sharp scissors in one cut.
Fix and stabilize the head using anchoring forceps at orbital cavities.
Collect 3–4 pups' brains in a 15 mL tube containing 1× HBSS solution.
Make an incision in the skin at the hindbrain along the midline to eye level.
Grasp the skin on both sides with Dumont #5 forceps and pull it aside to reveal the skull.
Carefully cut the cranium starting from the neck where the vertebral foramen is located, extending anteriorly to the nose.
Make additional transverse cuts to the eye cavity.
Cut the cranium carefully without applying excess pressure to avoid deformation of brain tissue and bleeding.
Use forceps to gently pull apart the cranium to reveal the brain.
Place a small spatula under the cerebellum and push it towards the olfactory bulbs.
Gently lift with the spatula to scoop out the brain.
Transfer the brain to a 10 cm petri dish containing ice-cold 1× HBSS under sterile conditions.
Submerge the brain completely in the liquid.
Remove olfactory bulbs to free the meninges.
Distinguish meninges by their reddish color from blood vessels.
Reverse the brain and start removing meninges from the bottom side.
Dissect the meninges from the surface of the cortical layer using fine forceps.
Flip the brain and continue removing meninges.
Check for meninges residue in the brain tissue.
Cut the brain into 6–10 pieces using forceps or sharp blades if no meninges are present.
Place the brain pieces into a 15 mL tube containing 10 mL of 1× HBSS.
Keep the tube on ice.
Under sterile conditions, add ice cold 0.05% DNase I into the tube.
Gently triturate brain tissue 10–15 times with a 10 mL and 2 mL pipette, respectively.
Add 0.05% trypsin to the mixture.
Mix by using a 10 mL pipette 20–30 times.
Incubate at room temperature (22°C–25°C) for 20 min.
Prepare one T-75 flask for each group of brains and coat with 3 mL of 0.01% Poly-L-Lysine (PLL).
Place the T-75 flask in the incubator.
Mix the Falcon tube thoroughly after 20 minutes of trypsin incubation.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 150 RCF to pellet brain tissue.
Aspirate the supernatant using a Pasteur pipette connected to a pump.
Resuspend the pellet with 2 mL of complete growth medium and repeat centrifugation step.
Resuspend cell pellet with 2-4 mL of DMEM using a 10 mL pipette.
Mix thoroughly 10-20 times to obtain a single-cell suspension.
Aspirate PLL from the T-75 flask and rinse with 10 mL of DMEM.
Add 8-10 mL of pre-warmed 37°C DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS and 2% pen/strep.
Plate the resuspended cell pellet.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 in an incubator.
Change the medium on day 1, day 2, and day 7 after plating the primary cells.
Wash the plate by using 1× PBS to remove unattached and dead cells before adding fresh complete growth medium.
Gently tap the flask from both sides several times when mixed cell culture reach confluency.
Check the cells under the microscope after tapping the flask.
Aspirate the medium completely to remove detached OPCs.
Rinse remaining cells carefully with 10 mL of complete growth medium.
Add 10 mL of complete growth medium and ice cold 0.5 mL DNase I to loosen the remaining cell layer.
Incubate for 5 min at 37°C with 5% CO2 in an incubator.
Release remaining OPCs by shaking the T-75 Flask horizontally 20–30 times.
Hold the shaken flask vertically for 30 seconds to allow foam to rise to the top.
Aspirate any remaining medium that may contain OPCs.
Wash the astrocytes and microglia layer with 3–4 mL of PBS.
Add 3–4 mL of 0.05% trypsin to the cells.
Incubate the flask for 3–5 minutes at 37°C with 5% CO2 in an incubator.
Check under a microscope for incomplete detachment, and tap the slide if necessary.
After checking, add 6–7 mL of complete growth medium to resuspend the cells.
Transfer the cell suspension to a new 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 150 rcf for 10 minutes.
Prepare 4 sterile 10-cm bacterial grade plates during centrifugation.
Add 2 mL of complete growth medium to each plate.
Aspirate the supernatant obtained after step 33.
Resuspend cells with 4 mL of complete growth medium.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension to each petri dish.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 20 min.
Collect all supernatants containing astrocytes from the 4 Petri dishes.
Pool the collected supernatant into a new 10-cm bacterial grade plate.
Tilt the plate gently and collect the supernatant carefully without shaking.
Incubate the pooled supernatant at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 90 min.
Check the cells under the microscope after incubation.
Transfer the supernatant containing primary astrocytes into a new T-75 flask.
Add additional amount of pre-warmed complete growth medium to fill up to 20 mL in the T-75 flask according to volume of the obtained supernatant.
Incubate the primary astrocytes for 7–15 days at 37°C with 5% CO2 in the incubator.

Change the complete growth medium by aspirating half of the old medium (approx. 10 mL) and replacing it with a fresh, pre-warmed complete growth medium (approx. 10 mL) every 4 days during cultivation.
Coat the μ-Slide 4 Well chamber with 300 μL of fibronectin at 5 μg/mL for 1 hour at 37°C.
Remove the fibronectin and wash the wells once with 500 μL of sterile PBS or water.
Place the washed chamber in the incubator to dry it.
Wash primary astrocytes when they reach confluency using 1× PBS.
Add 3 mL of 0.05% trypsin for 5 minutes at 37°C to detach cells.
Collect detached cells in a 15 mL tube and add 1–5 mL of growth media to prepare cell suspension.
Count the number of cells and prepare a 5 × 10^4 cells/mL suspension.
Add 700 μL (∼35,000 cells) of cell suspension into each well and incubate for 1 day at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Change the medium to fresh 700 μL of complete growth medium the next day.
Prepare 1 Eppendorf tube and add 100 μL of Opti-MEMTM.
Add 6 μL of GeneJuice® to the Eppendorf tube.
Vortex the solution thoroughly to mix it.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 5 min.
Add 2 μL of focal adhesion construct at a concentration of 1 μg/mL into the serum-free/GeneJuice® mixture.
Mix the solution by tapping the tubes gently, avoid vortexing.
Incubate the DNA-containing mixture at room temperature for 15 min.
Drop-wise add 27 μL of reagent/DNA mixture to the cells.
Rock the chamber to homogenize the solution in the complete growth medium.
After 24 h of transfection, remove the old medium containing transfection reagent.
Add pre-warmed complete growth medium to the cells.
Incubate the cells for an additional 24 h at 37°C with 5% CO2 in the incubator.
Before starting live-cell imaging, turn on the temperature and CO2 controller of Nikon Eclipse Ti2-E/Yokogawa CSU-W1 Spinning disk microscope.
Wait until the conditions stabilize before usage.
Acquire movies at 1 frame every 3 to 5 min with 20 z-stacks at a 0.5 μm step size for a time course of 1.25 h to 3 h.
Maintain consistent settings for all movie acquisitions to ensure experimental consistency.
Apply maximum projections to the movies.
Analyze focal adhesion assembly/disassembly rates using Focal Adhesion Analysis Server (FAAS).
Prepare 10 mm glass coverslips in 6-well plates and coat with fibronectin as described.
Seed 1–1.5 × 10^5 cells in each well and incubate the primary astrocytes cells for 48 h at 37°C with 5% CO2 in the incubator.
Remove the growth medium after the 48-hour incubation.
Wash the cells once quickly with 1× PBS.
Wash the cells a second time using 1× PBS for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Prepare a parafilm sheet and place it in a wet chamber to maintain humidity during incubation times.
Take the coverslips out of the wells and place them on the parafilm sheet.
Fix the cells by adding 50 μL of 2% PFA in 1× PBS for each coverslip for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the cells twice with 1× PBS, each for 10 minutes to remove remaining PFA.
Permeabilize the cells using 50 μL of 0.2% Triton-X-100 in PBS solution.
Remove the permeabilization solution and wash the cells with 50 μL of 50 mM NH4Cl in PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Incubate the cells with 50 μL of blocking solution (0.1% Ovalbumin and 0.5% Fish gelatin in 1× PBS) for 60 minutes at room temperature.

Treat the cells with 50 μL of primary antibodies (rabbit anti-GFAP at a dilution of 1:400 and mouse anti-vinculin at 1:200) prepared in blocking solution, either overnight at 4°C or for 2–3 hours at room temperature.
Wash the cells with 1× PBS once quickly after primary antibody incubation.
Wash the cells twice more with 1× PBS for 10 minutes each.
Apply 50 μL of secondary antibodies for each coverslip.
Incubate the cells with antibodies at room temperature for 60–75 min.
Wash the cells with 1× PBS one time rapidly.
Wash the cells with 1× PBS three times for 10 min.
Mount the coverslips with Mowiol.
Open the images using ImageJ software.
If Z-projection is not created, go to Image-Stacks-Z Project-Maximum Projection.
Save the processed image in the folder.
Pick an exported and processed image from the images folder.
To set the scale: First, draw a straight line on the image scale bar.
Go to Analyze-Set scale And mark as global.
Verify the scale by drawing a line on the scale bar.
Make a duplicate image named DUP1 for the RGB image (for comparison).
Draw a scale bar in the image near to the cell to be cropped.
Analyze-Tools-Scale bar
Now, select the Rectangle box symbol from the ImageJ toolbar and draw around the cell.
Then right-click within the drawn box and press duplicate.
Go to Image-Adjust-Brightness and contrast for adjustments and then save the image in the folder.
Again, go to 1st duplicate RGB image and again right-click within yellow box for the FFT image.
Separate the merged imaged Go to Image-Color-Split channels
And pick the channels which contain focal adhesion staining
To acquire the FFT image, change the RGB image to an 8-bit image.
Set pixel size for large structure to 20 pixels and small structure to 1 pixel.
Adjust tolerance of direction to 5%.
Select Autoscale after filtering.
Select Saturate image when autoscaling.
Press OK.
Go to Image-Adjust-Brightness Adjust brightness until the background turns black.
Save the Min/Max values for applying to other images.
Adjust maximum & then minimum.
Save the FFT filtered image.
Duplicate image.
Convert duplicate image to RGB color mode.
Close RGB image.
Go to Image-Adjust-Threshold Select Dark Background.
In first drop-down box select-Huang method.
In the second drop-down box select-B&W method.
Apply thresholding.
Run analyze particles.
Set the parameter for size: 40-Infinity and for circularity 0.00–0.99.
Select pixel units and show the outlines option.
Select display results, clear results, summarize & include holes.
Quantification of focal adhesion numbers per cell area.
Open the image with F-actin staining.
Draw a line around the cell body using the freehand tool in ImageJ toolbar.
Press control+M to get the area of the cell body.
Save the results.
Transfer the data to an Excel file.
Count the number of focal adhesions and divide it by the total cell area.
Use Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon Test for the significant test.
